# grapheme

```go
import "github.com/engmtcdrm/go-pardon/grapheme"
```

<a name="Equal"></a>
## func [Equal](<https://github.com/engmtcdrm/go-pardon/blob/main/grapheme/utils.go#L7>)

```go
func Equal(a Cluster, b Cluster) bool
```

Equal reports whether a and b are the same length and contain the same runes. A nil argument is equivalent to an empty slice.

<a name="EqualFold"></a>
## func [EqualFold](<https://github.com/engmtcdrm/go-pardon/blob/main/grapheme/utils.go#L14>)

```go
func EqualFold(a Cluster, b Cluster) bool
```

EqualFold reports whether a and b, interpreted as UTF\-8 strings, are equal under simple Unicode case\-folding, which is a more general form of case\-insensitivity.

```go
func HasSequenceEnd(gc Cluster) bool
```

HasSequenceEnd checks if the given Cluster contains a ANSI escape sequence end character.

<a name="IndexOfSequenceEnd"></a>
## func [IndexOfSequenceEnd](<https://github.com/engmtcdrm/go-pardon/blob/main/grapheme/utils.go#L32>)

```go
func IndexOfSequenceEnd(gc Cluster) int
```

IndexOfSequenceEnd returns the index of the ANSI escape sequence end character in the given Cluster, or \-1 if there is no such character.

<a name="Cluster"></a>
## type [Cluster](<https://github.com/engmtcdrm/go-pardon/blob/main/grapheme/cluster.go#L7>)

Cluster represents a grapheme cluster in a sequence of runes that form a single user\-perceived character, such as an emoji or a combined character. It is used to handle complex input scenarios where multiple runes may be combined into a single visual unit.

```go
type Cluster []rune
```
